svg.title: Customer segmentation pipeline
svg.desc: 2,240 customers are cleaned down to 2,191, K-Means finds 6 spending profiles shown as bubbles by income and wine spend, a KNN model predicts whether a new customer spends a lot on wine, and an honest evaluation gives about 92 % accuracy against a 50 % baseline, instead of the 99 % reported with data leakage.

g.text: 2 years of spend by category, campaigns
Drop odd labels and extreme meat spend
Birth year → age · kids + teens → children
k chosen with the elbow method
Each bubble on the right is a real centroid:
income vs. wine spend, area = share of customers.
Target: wine spend above the median (50 / 50).
Wine spend and the cluster label are left out,
The notebook fed wine spend and the cluster
back into the model; the fix removes them.

svg.text: Names are my interpretation of each profile's averages.

g.text: 2,240 customers from a public marketing dataset
Cleaning: nulls, outliers, text → numbers · 2,191 customers left
K-Means groups them into 6 spending profiles
KNN predicts a big wine buyer from everything except wine
